estimand.contrast_label: pooled MAPE for the mechanistic model minus pooled MAPE for the O-trained level-only comparator
estimand.short_contrast_label: pooled MAPE, mechanistic model − O-trained level-only comparator
estimand.direction_clause: negative values favour the mechanistic model
estimand.zero_means: equal pooled MAPE under the stated scoring rule
estimand.prose: pooled MAPE for the mechanistic model minus pooled MAPE for the O-trained level-only comparator, in percentage points; negative values favour the mechanistic model

resampling_design.estimand_support: observation-weighted mean over the complete held-out C/F observation corpus

cond_in_variety.name: cond_in_variety
cond_in_variety.label: (variety, temperature, pressure) condition, resampled within variety
cond_in_variety.rationale: keeps all three co-measured solutes at a condition together and, where both grinds exist, additionally moves the distinct C and F sample records together. This is a deliberately conservative dependence assumption, not a uniquely identified experimental sampling unit.

sample_in_variety_grind.name: sample_in_variety_grind
sample_in_variety_grind.label: sample record, resampled within variety x grind
sample_in_variety_grind.rationale: one cluster per coffee sample record, carrying the three solute outcomes measured from that sample. This is the dependency the source establishes most directly.

cond_in_group.name: cond_in_group
cond_in_group.label: (temperature, pressure) condition within variety x solute group
cond_in_group.rationale: keeps C and F together for one solute but lets different solutes of a variety draw different conditions, so it does not preserve cross-solute condition dependence.

group.name: group
group.label: whole variety x solute group
group.rationale: the coarsest construction: six clusters only, so its percentile distribution is highly discrete. Reported as a stress test, not as a high-resolution analysis.

stability_audits.scope: multi-seed Monte Carlo precision audit of the 40 g, cond_in_variety, primary fitting loss clustered percentile bounds; applies to no other endpoint, scheme or fitting loss
stability_audits.interpretation: Monte Carlo stability of the resampling percentiles only. This is numerical approximation error, not sampling uncertainty, and confers no coverage interpretation on the range. The third displayed decimal is resolved only to within the reported Monte Carlo standard error.

estimand: pooled held-out MAPE of the frozen optimal-grind mechanistic calibration MINUS that of the optimal-grind-trained level-only constant, both evaluated at the same matched-mass endpoint, over the declared held-out coarse/fine corpus
reading: Across the 38/40/42 g collected-mass sweep the paired model-minus-comparator difference stays stable in sign at about -0.447 to -0.394 pp. Whether the primary clustered sensitivity range's boundary sits on the negative side of zero CHANGES across the sweep. These are fixed-predictor sensitivity ranges without calibrated coverage, so neither outcome is evidence of statistical superiority or non-superiority.
note: This is NOT the same quantity as `endpoint_mass_sensitivity`, which reports the blind optimal-grind per-condition residual. Both predictors are re-derived at each endpoint here, so a shift common to both cancels -- which is exactly why the ~5 pp movement in the blind residual does not by itself imply that the model-versus-comparator conclusion is endpoint-dependent.
